feed.title: NPR Programs: All Things Considered
feed.subtitle: All Things Considered hosts Ailsa Chang, Mary Louise Kelly, Juana Summers and Scott Detrow present the program's trademark mix of news, interviews, commentaries, reviews, and offbeat features 7 days a week.

entry.title: The Nancy Grace Roman Telescope begins its journey into deep space
entry.summary: NASA launched a telescope named after Nancy Grace Roman, the pioneering astronomer whose work helped make Hubble and generations of space telescopes possible.

entry.title: Finally, an economic indicator you can eat
entry.summary: A corn dog may look like lunch. But to an economist, the price is a bigger story about food prices and inflation.

entry.title: Getting aid to Nepal's flood survivors is the next challenge
entry.summary: The U.S. has pledged 3.5 million in flood aid for Tibet and Nepal, with the first $500,000 distributed by Catholic Relief Services. An aid worker with the group explains what flood survivors need now.

entry.title: Insanity defenses rarely work. Lindsay Clancy's case may be different
entry.summary: Insanity defenses are notoriously difficult to win. But Massachusetts law could give Lindsay Clancy a better chance.

entry.title: Noel Godin, who made powerful people nervous around cream pies, dies at 80
entry.summary: For more than 50 years, Noel Godin went after famous and powerful people with cream pies. His targets included politicians, philosophers, filmmakers and, famously, Bill Gates.

entry.title: Cineplexity: When singers become movie stars
entry.summary: Dolly Parton built a movie career on top of an already huge music career. Other singers have tried, with mixed results.

entry.title: What a Brazilian tradition can teach us about the future of psychedelics
entry.summary: Researchers are looking at new ways to use psychedelics to treat depression. Science journalist Marcelo Leite says there's also a lot to learn from indigenous people who have used them for generations.

entry.title: The Ukrainian women disappearing into Russian prisons
entry.summary: What happens when Russia arrests civilians in the Ukrainian territories it occupies? New Yorker writer Joshua Yaffa followed a group of women through the Russian prison system.

entry.title: He offered strangers $10 to tie his shoe. Then things got weird
entry.summary: Would $10 convince you to walk up to a stranger and tie their shoe? One Minneapolis artist turned that question into delightfully public chaos.

entry.title: Trump says U.S. has struck a deal for control of Venezuelan oil reserves
entry.summary: President Trump says a new deal with Venezuela would give the U.S. control of more than 65 billion barrels of oil reserves.
